questions.figure_locator: Page 7, Item 19 (vertical hoop geometry with bottom anchor)
questions.solver_solution: Top of hoop: height = 2R, spring length = 2R (extension = R), K_i = 0. Total E_i = mg(2R) + 1/2 k R^2. When spring length = R, bead form equilateral triangle with bottom and center, height = R(1 - cos 60°) = 0.5R, spring extension = 0. Total E_f = mg(0.5R) + 1/2 m v^2. Equating: 1/2 m v^2 = 1.5 mgR + 1/2 k R^2 => v = \sqrt{3gR + kR^2/m}.

questions.raw_stem: A block of mass $25\text{ kg}$ is pulled along a rough horizontal surface by a force directed at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the horizontal. questions.normalized_stem: A block of mass $25\text{ kg}$ is pulled along a rough horizontal surface by a force directed at an angle of $45^\circ$ above the horizontal. questions.solver_solution: Vertical balance: N = mg - F sin 45°. Constant velocity horizontal balance: F cos 45° = \mu N = 0.25 (25 * 9.8 - F sin 45°). F(1/\sqrt{2}) = 0.25 * 245 - 0.25 * F(1/\sqrt{2}) => 1.25 F / \sqrt{2} = 61.25 => F = 49 \sqrt{2} N. Work W = F d cos 45° = (49 \sqrt{2}) * 5 * (1/\sqrt{2}) = 245 J.

binding.band_reason: Connects modified normal force to friction balance and constant velocity equilibrium before computing work via dot product.
binding.crux: Account for reduction of normal reaction by oblique component before finding friction and computing W = F d cos \theta.

questions.raw_stem: A block of mass $1\text{ kg}$ is kept on an inclined plane with $30^\circ$ inclination with respect to the horizontal and it is at rest relative to the incline. Then the whole assembly is moved vertically upward with a constant velocity of $4\text{ m/s}$. The work done by the frictional force on the block in time $2\text{ s}$ is: (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.normalized_stem: A block of mass $1\text{ kg}$ is kept on an inclined plane with $30^\circ$ inclination with respect to the horizontal and it is at rest relative to the incline. questions.raw_stem: A bullet of mass $0.1\text{ kg}$ moving horizontally with a speed of $400\text{ m s}^{-1}$ hits a wooden block of mass $3.9\text{ kg}$ kept on a horizontal rough surface. questions.normalized_stem: A bullet of mass $0.1\text{ kg}$ moving horizontally with a speed of $400\text{ m s}^{-1}$ hits a wooden block of mass $3.9\text{ kg}$ kept on a horizontal rough surface. questions.solver_solution: Inelastic collision: m v_0 = (m + M) V => 0.1 * 400 = 4.0 * V => V = 10 m/s. Work-energy theorem on rough surface: W_f = \Delta K => -\mu (m+M) g s = 0 - 1/2 (m+M) V^2 => \mu = V^2 / (2 g s) = 100 / (2 * 10 * 20) = 0.25.

binding.crux: Chain inelastic momentum conservation to obtain post-collision velocity and apply work done by friction W_f = -\Delta K to solve for \mu.
